+ combining argument: a placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism, placements on
+ opposite register pairs commute, and the crosswise exchange of the two EPR
+ pairs of the expanded state carries the placement `AA'` to `AB''` and `BA''`
+ to `BB'` while fixing the expanded state.  The last fact transfers every
+ state-dependent distance between the two bipartition schemes of
+ `def:symmetric-equivalents` without assuming a symmetric strategy.
+ 
+ ## References
+ 
+ The placements are those of `def:symmetric-equivalents`, blueprint
+ `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, paper
+ `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`.
+ The EPR-exchange invariance is proved directly for the involution
+ `(A' B'')(A'' B')`, which fixes the strategy registers.  Its use for
+ `lem:qld-4-10` is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
+ -/
+ 
+ open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+ 
+ namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+ 
+ open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
+ open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+ 
+ noncomputable section
+ 
+ namespace ProjectiveSetting
+ 
+ variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
+ 
+ /-! ## Placements as reindexed tensor factors -/
+ 
+ /-- The `AA'` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
+ `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
+ theorem place_AA'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AA'.side)) :
+     S.place .AA' O =
+       reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+         (heteroKron O
+           (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
+             (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
+   (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_left S O).symm
+ 
+ /-- The `BA''` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
+ `AA' | BA''(B'B'')` bipartition. -/
+ theorem place_BA''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BA''.side)) :
+     S.place .BA'' O =
+       reindexOp (aaBaBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+         (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
+           (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
+   (reindexOp_aaBaBipartition_right S O).symm
+ 
+ /-- The `AB''` placement is the reindexed left factor of the
+ `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
+ theorem place_AB''_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.AB''.side)) :
+     S.place .AB'' O =
+       reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+         (heteroKron O
+           (1 : Op ((S.toStrategy.ιB × PauliRegister P) ×
+             (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
+   (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_left S O).symm
+ 
+ /-- The `BB'` placement is the reindexed right factor of the
+ `AB'' | BB'(A'A'')` bipartition. -/
+ theorem place_BB'_eq (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace Placement.BB'.side)) :
+     S.place .BB' O =
+       reindexOp (abBbBipartition P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+         (heteroKron (1 : Op (S.toStrategy.ιA × PauliRegister P))
+           (heteroKron O (1 : Op (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)))) :=
+   (reindexOp_abBbBipartition_right S O).symm
+ 
+ /-- Reindexing an operator commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
+ theorem reindexOp_conjTranspose {ι κ : Type*} (e : ι ≃ κ) (M : Op κ) :
+     reindexOp e Mᴴ = (reindexOp e M)ᴴ := by
+   ext i j
+   rfl
+ 
+ /-- Reindexing an operator along an equivalence preserves positivity. -/
+ theorem reindexOp_nonneg {ι κ : Type*} [Finite ι] [Finite κ]
+     (e : ι ≃ κ) {M : Op κ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) :
+     0 ≤ reindexOp e M := by
+   letI := Fintype.ofFinite ι
+   letI := Fintype.ofFinite κ
+   rw [Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef] at hM ⊢
+   exact hM.submatrix e.symm.symm
+ 
+ /-! ## The placement is a unital `*`-homomorphism -/
+ 
+ set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
+ /-- A placement is multiplicative. -/
+ theorem place_mul (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+     ∀ (p : Placement) (A B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
+       S.place p (A * B) = S.place p A * S.place p B
+   | .AA', A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .BA'', A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
+         mul_one, mul_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .BB', A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, heteroKron_mul,
+         mul_one, mul_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .AB'', A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul, heteroKron_mul, mul_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+ 
+ /-- A placement sends the local identity to the identity of the six-register
+ space. -/
+ theorem place_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) :
+     S.place p (1 : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) = 1 := by
+   ext i j
+   cases p <;>
+     · simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.one_apply, Prod.ext_iff]
+       split_ifs <;> simp_all
+ 
+ /-- A placement is additive over finite sums of local operators. -/
+ theorem place_finsetSum (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {γ : Type*}
+     (s : Finset γ) (O : γ → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
+     S.place p (∑ x ∈ s, O x) = ∑ x ∈ s, S.place p (O x) := by
+   ext i j
+   cases p <;>
+     simp only [ProjectiveSetting.place, Matrix.sum_apply, Finset.sum_mul,
+       Finset.mul_sum]
+ 
+ /-- A placement commutes with the conjugate transpose. -/
+ theorem place_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+     ∀ (p : Placement) (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)),
+       S.place p Aᴴ = (S.place p A)ᴴ
+   | .AA', A => by
+       rw [place_AA'_eq, place_AA'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .BA'', A => by
+       rw [place_BA''_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
+         Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .BB', A => by
+       rw [place_BB'_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
+         Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+   | .AB'', A => by
+       rw [place_AB''_eq, place_AB''_eq, ← reindexOp_conjTranspose,
+         WinImplications.heteroKron_conjTranspose, Matrix.conjTranspose_one]
+       all_goals rfl
+ 
+ set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
+ /-- A placement preserves positivity. -/
+ theorem place_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+     ∀ (p : Placement) {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)}, 0 ≤ A →
+       0 ≤ S.place p A
+   | .AA', A, hA => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AA'_eq]
+       exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA
+         (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg))
+   | .BA'', A, hA => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_BA''_eq]
+       exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
+         (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
+         (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)))
+   | .BB', A, hA => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_BB'_eq]
+       exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
+         (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)
+         (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg)))
+   | .AB'', A, hA => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AB''_eq]
+       exact reindexOp_nonneg _ (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg hA
+         (Matrix.PosSemidef.one.nonneg))
+ 
+ /-- The placement of a local operator bounded by the identity is bounded by
+ the identity. -/
+ theorem place_le_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
+     {A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hA : A ≤ 1) :
+     S.place p A ≤ 1 := by
+   have h : 0 ≤ S.place p (1 - A) := S.place_nonneg p (sub_nonneg.mpr hA)
+   rw [place_sub, place_one] at h
+   exact sub_nonneg.mp h
+ 
+ /-- The placement of a projector is a contraction. -/
+ theorem place_conjTranspose_mul_self_le_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (p : Placement) {E : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)} (hE : IsProj E) :
+     (S.place p E)ᴴ * S.place p E ≤ 1 := by
+   rw [← place_conjTranspose, ← place_mul, hE.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
+     hE.isIdempotentElem.eq]
+   exact S.place_le_one p (sub_nonneg.mp hE.one_sub.nonneg)
+ 
+ set_option synthInstance.maxSize 400 in
+ /-- Operators placed on opposite register pairs commute. -/
+ theorem place_comm (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+     ∀ (p₁ p₂ : Placement), p₁.IsOpposite p₂ →
+       ∀ (A : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₁.side))
+         (B : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p₂.side)),
+         S.place p₁ A * S.place p₂ B = S.place p₂ B * S.place p₁ A
+   | .AA', .BA'', _, A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AA'_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
+       simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
+   | .BA'', .AA', _, A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AA'_eq, place_BA''_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
+       simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
+   | .BB', .AB'', _, A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AB''_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
+       simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
+   | .AB'', .BB', _, A, B => by
+       classical
+       rw [place_AB''_eq, place_BB'_eq, ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul,
+         ← WinImplications.reindexOp_mul]
+       simp only [heteroKron_mul, one_mul, mul_one]
+   | .AA', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .AA', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .AA', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BA'', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BA'', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BA'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BB', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BB', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .BB', .BB', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .AB'', .AA', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .AB'', .BA'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+   | .AB'', .AB'', h, _, _ => by simp [Placement.IsOpposite] at h
+ 
+ /-- A complete measurement on a local expanded space, placed on one of the
+ four register pairs, is a complete measurement on the six-register space. -/
+ def placedMeasurement (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement) {α : Type*}
+     [Fintype α] (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
+     Measurement α (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
+   Measurement.ofSumEqOne (fun a => S.place p (M.effect a))
+     (fun a => S.place_nonneg p (M.pos a))
+     (by rw [← place_finsetSum, M.sum_eq_one, place_one])
+ 
+ /-- The effects of a placed measurement are the placed effects. -/
+ @[simp] theorem placedMeasurement_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
+     (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) (a : α) :
+     (S.placedMeasurement p M).effect a = S.place p (M.effect a) := rfl
+ 
+ /-- A placed projective measurement is projective. -/
+ theorem placedMeasurement_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (p : Placement) {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
+     (M : Measurement α (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side))
+     (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
+     MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.placedMeasurement p M) := by
+   intro a
+   refine isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩
+   · change S.place p (M.effect a) * S.place p (M.effect a) =
+       S.place p (M.effect a)
+     rw [← place_mul, (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
+   · change star (S.place p (M.effect a)) = S.place p (M.effect a)
+     rw [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, ← place_conjTranspose,
+       (hM a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
+ 
+ /-! ## The crosswise exchange of the two EPR pairs -/
+ 
+ /-- The permutation of the six registers exchanging `A'` with `B''` and `A''`
+ with `B'`, while fixing `A` and `B`.  This involution exchanges the two EPR
+ pairs and reverses the order within each pair. -/
+ def eprCrossSwap (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
+     SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
+   toFun := fun ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ => ((a, (b'', b')), (b, (a'', a')))
+   invFun := fun ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ => ((a, (b'', b')), (b, (a'', a')))
+   left_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩; rfl
+   right_inv := by rintro ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩; rfl
+ 
+ /-- The EPR vector is symmetric in its two registers. -/
+ theorem eprState_ofLp_swap {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
+     [Nonempty V] (x y : V) :
+     (eprState V).ofLp (x, y) = (eprState V).ofLp (y, x) := by
+   change (if x = y then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0) =
+     (if y = x then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
+   by_cases h : x = y
+   · simp [h]
+   · simp [h, Ne.symm h]
+ 
+ /-- The crosswise EPR exchange fixes the expanded state: the two EPR factors
+ are identical and each is symmetric under exchange of its registers.  No
+ symmetry of the strategy state is required. -/
+ theorem reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
+     reindexState (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) S.psiHat =
+       S.psiHat := by
+   ext i
+   obtain ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ := i
+   change S.toStrategy.ψ.ofLp (a, b) * (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (b'', b') *
+       (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (a'', a') =
+     S.toStrategy.ψ.ofLp (a, b) * (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (a', a'') *
+       (eprState (PauliRegister P)).ofLp (b', b'')
+   rw [eprState_ofLp_swap b'' b', eprState_ofLp_swap a'' a']
+   ring
+ 
+ /-- The crosswise EPR exchange carries the `AB''` placement to the `AA'`
+ placement. -/
+ theorem reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_AB'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
+     reindexOp (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+       (S.place .AB'' O) = S.place .AA' O := by
+   ext i j
+   obtain ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ := i
+   obtain ⟨⟨c, c', c''⟩, d, d', d''⟩ := j
+   simp only [reindexOp, Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
+     Equiv.symm_symm, place, eprCrossSwap, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Matrix.one_apply]
+   ring!
+ 
+ /-- The crosswise EPR exchange carries the `BB'` placement to the `BA''`
+ placement. -/
+ theorem reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_BB' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
+     reindexOp (eprCrossSwap P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+       (S.place .BB' O) = S.place .BA'' O := by
+   ext i j
+   obtain ⟨⟨a, a', a''⟩, b, b', b''⟩ := i
+   obtain ⟨⟨c, c', c''⟩, d, d', d''⟩ := j
+   simp only [reindexOp, Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
+     Equiv.symm_symm, place, eprCrossSwap, Equiv.coe_fn_mk, Matrix.one_apply]
+   ring!
+ 
+ /-- An operator placed on `AB''` has, on the expanded state, the same norm as
+ the same operator placed on `AA'`, by invariance under the crosswise EPR
+ exchange. -/
+ theorem norm_place_AB''_eq_norm_place_AA' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
+     ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .AB'' O) S.psiHat‖ =
+       ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .AA' O) S.psiHat‖ := by
+   conv_lhs => rw [← reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat S]
+   rw [WinImplications.norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState,
+     reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_AB'']
+ 
+ /-- An operator placed on `BB'` has, on the expanded state, the same norm as
+ the same operator placed on `BA''`, by invariance under the crosswise EPR
+ exchange. -/
+ theorem norm_place_BB'_eq_norm_place_BA'' (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
+     (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
+     ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .BB' O) S.psiHat‖ =
+       ‖applyOperatorToState (S.place .BA'' O) S.psiHat‖ := by
+   conv_lhs => rw [← reindexState_eprCrossSwap_psiHat S]
+   rw [WinImplications.norm_applyOperatorToState_reindexState,
+     reindexOp_eprCrossSwap_place_BB']
+ 
+ /-- Transfer of a same-side state-dependent distance between the `AA'` and
+ `AB''` placements. -/
+ theorem opFamilyDistSq_place_AB''_eq_AA' {X α : Type*} [Fintype α]
+     (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (μ : Distribution X)
+     (A B : X → α → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice)) :
+     opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .AB'' (A x a))
+         (fun x a => S.place .AB'' (B x a)) S.psiHat =
+       opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .AA' (A x a))
+         (fun x a => S.place .AA' (B x a)) S.psiHat := by
+   unfold opFamilyDistSq
+   refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+   rw [← place_sub, ← place_sub, norm_place_AB''_eq_norm_place_AA']
+   all_goals rfl
+ 
+ /-- Transfer of a same-side state-dependent distance between the `BA''` and
+ `BB'` placements. -/
+ theorem opFamilyDistSq_place_BB'_eq_BA'' {X α : Type*} [Fintype α]
+     (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (μ : Distribution X)
+     (A B : X → α → Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob)) :
+     opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .BB' (A x a))
+         (fun x a => S.place .BB' (B x a)) S.psiHat =
+       opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => S.place .BA'' (A x a))
+         (fun x a => S.place .BA'' (B x a)) S.psiHat := by
+   unfold opFamilyDistSq
+   refine avgOver_congr _ _ _ fun x => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
+   rw [← place_sub, ← place_sub, norm_place_BB'_eq_norm_place_BA'']
+   all_goals rfl
+ 
+ end ProjectiveSetting
+ 
+ end
+ 
+ end MIPStarRE.QPBT

 +/-!
 +# The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
 +
 +The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
 +measurements into the sandwich POVM
 +`R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
 +source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
 +outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
 +`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
 +defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
 +`M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
 +the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
 +the self-consistency of each factor.
 +
 +## Main results

 +* `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
 +* `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
 +  product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
 +* `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
 +  the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
 +

 +`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960` (`lem:qld-4-10`); the
 +route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`.

 +/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
 +theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
 +    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
 +    (a : PauliScalar P) :
 +    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
 +  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq
 +
 +/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
 +theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
 +    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
 +    (a : PauliScalar P) :
 +    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
 +      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
 +  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq
 +
 +/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
 +theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
 +    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
 +    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
 +      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
 +        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
 +  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
 +    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
 +      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
 +    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
 +      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
 +    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]
 +
 +/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
 +theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
 +    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
 +    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
 +  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
 +  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
 +      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
 +          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
 +        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
 +        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
 +    _ = 1 := by
 +        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
 +          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
 +        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one
 +
 +/-- The sandwich POVM `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` of the two expanded
 +point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
 +first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
 +`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,
 +formed directly with field-valued outcomes rather than from the binary
 +refinements; see `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation.tex`. -/
 +def sandwichPoint (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
 +    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
 +    Measurement (PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
 +  Measurement.ofSumEqOne
 +    (fun ab => (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +      (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
 +      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2)
 +    (fun ab => by
 +      rw [sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self]
 +      exact Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
 +        (Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self _))
 +    (sum_sandwich_eq_one S side x z)
 +
 +/-- The effects of the sandwich POVM. -/
 +@[simp] theorem sandwichPoint_effect (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
 +    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
 +    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
 +    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab =
 +      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 := rfl
 +
 +/-- The sandwich differs from the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` by
 +`M^Z_b` times the commutator.  This is the algebra behind display
 +`eq:qld-r-2`, paper
 +`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:737-742`. -/
 +theorem sandwichPoint_effect_sub_ordered (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
 +    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
 +    (ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P) :
 +    (S.sandwichPoint side x z).effect ab -
 +        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 =
 +      (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
 +            (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 -
 +          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
 +            (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1) := by
 +  rw [sandwichPoint_effect, mul_sub, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
 +    pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]

 +/-- The sandwich POVM is close to the ordered product `M^Z_b M^X_a` on every
 +register placement, on average over the point pair, with the error of
 +`lem:qld-comm-cons`.  This is display `eq:qld-r-2` of the proof of
 +`lem:qld-4-10`, paper

 +  obtain ⟨C, hC, h⟩ := expPoint_comm
 +  refine ⟨C, hC, fun P ε S p => le_trans ?_ (h P ε S p)⟩

 +  refine avgOver_mono _ _ _ fun xz => Finset.sum_le_sum fun ab _ => ?_

+ # The sandwich POVM of the expanded point measurements
+ 
+ The first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10` combines the two expanded point
+ measurements into the sandwich POVM
+ `R^{x,z}_{a,b} = M^{(Point,Z),z}_b M^{(Point,X),x}_a M^{(Point,Z),z}_b`.  The
+ source forms it from the binary refinements; here it is formed directly with
+ outcomes in `F_q × F_q`, which the Parseval transfer of
+ `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Commutation.lean` makes possible.  This file
+ defines the POVM, proves that it is close to the ordered product
+ `M^Z_b M^X_a` by the approximate commutation, and records the consistency of
+ the ordered products across opposite register placements, which follows from
+ the self-consistency of each factor.
+ 
+ ## Main results
+ 
+ * `ProjectiveSetting.sandwichPoint`: the sandwich POVM.
+ * `sandwichPoint_ordered_dist_le`: closeness of the sandwich to the ordered
+   product on every placement, with the error of `lem:qld-comm-cons`.
+ * `ordered_cross_dist_le`: the ordered product on one placement is close to
+   the reversed ordered product on the opposite placement.
+ 
+ ## References
+ 
+ Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-748`
+ (the sandwich and display `eq:qld-r-2`), blueprint
+ `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:803-960` (`lem:qld-4-10`); the
+ route is explained in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-points-direct.tex`.
+ -/

	\label{thm:linearity}
		Let $0 \leq \delta \leq 1$, let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\alice \otimes \mathcal{H}_\bob$. Normative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for
`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).

consumes but never writes.

`ci.sh <pr-number>` is the **only** thing allowed to publish the `local-ci/*`
commit statuses. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only
after green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit
failures are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads
those exact-head statuses and the manifest comment this script publishes
(`local/protocols/issues-prs.md` §2), and nothing else.

## 1. What it is

The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
invocation, one manifest, one exit code.

```
local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
```

`<pr-id>` is the GitHub PR number; the script reads `branch`, `base` and the
head SHA from GitHub (`gh_common.py pr-view`), finds the branch's worktree (via
`git worktree list`, falling back to `.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and
runs everything **inside that worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary
checkout, and the worktree's branch tip must equal the remote head before the
run starts.

Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
(unknown PR number, missing worktree, unresolvable base, GitHub unreachable —
a GitHub error never degrades to a local record).

### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips

| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
|---|---|
| GitHub returns an open PR with a head branch | there is no branch to test |
| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |
| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the "checks silently stopped running" failure the parent repo patched twice |
| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |
| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |

There is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`
and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green
light it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the head SHA simply
keeps whatever statuses it already carries.

Every step is blocking. The single advisory sub-check is
`check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`: exit 1 means "candidates reported" and is
downgraded to a warning, any other nonzero status is a real failure — the same
`set +e` dance as `pr-ci.yml:432-445`.

The PDF subpass invokes `latexmk` from `blueprint/src`, so the checked status is
the compiler driver's status rather than a wrapper's. It uses the checked-in
`latexmkrc` and adds `nonstopmode`, `halt-on-error`, and file-line diagnostics.
The command must return zero and create a non-empty `print.pdf` after the prior
artifact was removed. A fresh but partial PDF cannot replace a successful
compiler exit. The driver checks that status explicitly because the step
dispatcher disables `errexit` while capturing each outcome; later successful
bbl or web commands must never overwrite an earlier PDF failure.

Two GitHub-only behaviours are dropped on purpose: `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
blocks and `::error` / `::notice` / `::warning` annotations are inert outside
Actions, so the step's stdout+stderr log **is** the summary. `--github-annotations`
is not passed to `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`. Exit-code semantics are
preserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep
always did.

### Steps that did not run

A step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never
omitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped
GitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that
under-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.

## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep

`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces
`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old
and the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's
filter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching
minimatch's `**`.

| Area | Globs | Parent |
|---|---|---|
| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |
| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |
| `ldt_lean` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean` | `:91-92` |
| `blueprint` | `blueprint/*` | `:93-94` |
| `blueprint_src` | `blueprint/src/*` | `:95-96` |
| `tex_chapter` | `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` | `:97-98` |
| `paper_gaps` | `docs/paper-gaps/*`, `texra-blueprint.toml`, `MIPStarRE/*.lean`, `blueprint/src/*`, `docs/*.md` | `:99-107` |
| `scripts` | `scripts/*` | `:108-109` |
| `comparator` | `scripts/comparator/*` | `:110-111` |
| `workflow` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`, `local/bin/*`, `local/protocols/*`, `.githooks/*` | `:112-113`, extended |

> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit
> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice
> after checks silently never ran — the note at `pr-ci.yml:102-104` is the scar.
> The failure mode is asymmetric: an over-broad glob costs CPU, an under-broad
> glob costs a merged regression that no check ever looked at. When you widen
> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same
> commit, per `meta.md` §5.

The `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant "the
workflow file changed, so re-run everything"; locally the workflow layer is a
whole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under
`local/bin/`, every protocol under `local/protocols/`, and the hooks in
`.githooks/` — and a change to any of them forces a full run, every step
included. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has
to run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by
`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no
area and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).

## 4. Manifest schema

Built in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then
posted as the manifest PR comment (§5):

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run
```

A run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;
`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.

Step logs live outside the repository, under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.

```jsonc
{
  "schema": 1,
  "generator": "local/bin/ci.sh",
  "replaces": ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
  "pr": 7,                       // GitHub PR number
  "branch": "issue-7-qpbt-basis",
  "base": "main",                // from the GitHub PR
  "base_ref": "origin/main",     // what actually resolved
  "merge_base": "<sha>",
  "head_sha": "<sha>",           // the SHA every step ran against
  "worktree": "/abs/path",
  "started": "2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800",   // ISO-8601 with offset
  "finished": "2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800",
  "seconds": 1125,               // whole run, integer
  "conclusion": "success",       // success | failure | error
  "partial": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict
  "areas": { "lean": true, "blueprint_src": false, ... },
  "changed_files": ["MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean", ...],
  "warnings": ["texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...", ...],
  "steps": [
    {
      "step": "build",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight
      "outcome": "success",      // success | failure | error | skipped
      "seconds": 883,
      "log_path": "/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log",
      "blocking": true,
      "note": ""                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause
    }
  ]
}
```

`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\n\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run\n```\n\nA run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;\n`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\nper-file without serializing.\n\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\nthe lease directories by hand.\n\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\n\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\n\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\n   hard error.\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets\n   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that\n   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know\n   is clean.\n4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the\n   comparator drift check.\n\nEvery `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets\n`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`\nmake Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;\n`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any\norchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.\n\nLake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot\nolder than the merge base is safe — but only within one\n`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that\nboundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates\nthe check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.\n\n## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run\n\n`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. What the reviewer must return\n\nA single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state\nfield carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer\nin the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands\nthree things in order:\n\n1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:\n\n       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary\n\n   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of\n   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line\n   `- none`;\n2. a `## Review` section with the prose;\n3. as the final line, alone:\n\n       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED\n\nA missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,\nposts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section\nis discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a\n`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving\nverdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate\nstill blocks. # Absorption estimates for combined point measurements

This module proves the first projection step used to compare a joint point
measurement with the corresponding marginal point measurement.  Projectivity
makes the complementary projection contractive, and the two ordered
consistency fields of `CombinedPointsWitness` supply the resulting averaged
bounds.

## References

Paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:902-915`.

    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Quantum.Measurement α ι)
    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (a : α) (A D : Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    ‖applyOperatorToState (A - M.effect a * A) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ‖applyOperatorToState (A - M.effect a * D) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
  have hidem := (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq
  have hgram : (1 - M.effect a)ᴴ * (1 - M.effect a) ≤ 1 := by
    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_one,
      (hM a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
    calc
      (1 - M.effect a) * (1 - M.effect a) = 1 - M.effect a := by
        simp only [sub_mul, mul_sub, one_mul, mul_one, hidem]
        abel
      _ ≤ 1 := sub_le_self _ (M.pos a)
  have heq : A - M.effect a * A =
      (1 - M.effect a) * (A - M.effect a * D) := by
    simp only [sub_mul, mul_sub, one_mul, ← mul_assoc, hidem]
    abel
  rw [heq, DistanceCalculus.applyOperatorToState_mul]
  exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (norm_nonneg _)
    (MagicSquareRigidity.norm_applyOperatorToState_le hgram _) 2

/-- The joint point witness absorbs the opposite X point projector with
error at most its actual parameter. This is the X counterpart of the first
projection step of `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 902--915, obtained from
`consistent_XZ` rather than from an assumed marginal identity. -/
theorem CombinedPointsWitness.absorb_X_le {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
    (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopp : p1.IsOpposite p2) :
    opFamilyDistSq
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1) *
        S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)) S.psiHat ≤ δQ := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (points.consistent_XZ p1 p2 hopp)
  unfold opFamilyDistSq
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro xz
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro ab _
  simpa only [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect, ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]
    using norm_sub_projective_mul_sq_le
      (S.placedMeasurement p2 (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1))
      (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p2 _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
      ab.1 (S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2)) S.psiHat

/-- The joint point witness absorbs the opposite Z point projector with
error at most its actual parameter. This is the first projection step in
`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 902--915, derived from `consistent_ZX`. -/
theorem CombinedPointsWitness.absorb_Z_le {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
    {S : ProjectiveSetting P ε} (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
    (p1 p2 : Placement) (hopp : p1.IsOpposite p2) :
    opFamilyDistSq
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2) *
        S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab)) S.psiHat ≤ δQ := by
  refine le_trans ?_ (points.consistent_ZX p1 p2 hopp)
  unfold opFamilyDistSq
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro xz
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro ab _
  simpa only [ProjectiveSetting.placedMeasurement_effect, ProjectiveSetting.place_mul]
    using norm_sub_projective_mul_sq_le
      (S.placedMeasurement p2 (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2))
      (S.placedMeasurement_isProjective p2 _ (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective _ _ _))
      ab.2 (S.place p1 ((points.Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (S.place p2 ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1)) S.psiHat

end
